reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an Ulta Beauty gift-with-purchase promotion tied to a stated $19.50 retail purchase and focuses on trying and reviewing the included cosmetics. The ordinary subscribe request is not connected to a deceptive financial or data-collection mechanism.

citations.quote: Right now you can get a FREE 10 piece gift with any $19.50 ULTA Beauty purchase.
to get the free gift I needed to spend $19.50
we're gonna go ahead and try everything out
on Ulta's website it is still available
they had a ten piece ultra beauty gift set that you can get if you spend $19.50 or more

opening.argument: Judge the offer by the action it asks viewers to take. The headline promises ten free gifts, but the stated route to them is a qualifying purchase. The closing pitch makes that exchange explicit: go to the store, spend money, and receive the bundle. Calling the bundle free can obscure that viewers must buy something first. The promise and purchase request belong together when assessing whether this is a low-barrier reward solicitation.

citations.quote: GET 10 FREE Gifts @ ULTA Beauty RIGHT NOW!!!
Right now you can get a FREE 10 piece gift with any $19.50 ULTA Beauty purchase.
If your store has it, you need to run down to Ulta, something for $19 and get this whole stuff for free!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's purchase threshold does not make the reward pitch incidental; it identifies the action required to obtain it. Trying the products shows what the viewer is being encouraged to seek, while the closing instruction turns that demonstration into a request to spend. The subscribe request is not the relevant transaction. The gift-for-purchase appeal is.

citations.quote: Right now you can get a FREE 10 piece gift with any $19.50 ULTA Beauty purchase.
If your store has it, you need to run down to Ulta, something for $19 and get this whole stuff for free!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The condition is disclosed, not concealed: the description specifies a gift with a $19.50 purchase, and the speaker says she bought two brow pencils to qualify. A retail gift-with-purchase offer is not evidence that the purchase or reward is deceptive. The opening identifies a real incentive, but gives no basis to conclude viewers are misled about what they must do.

citations.quote: Right now you can get a FREE 10 piece gift with any $19.50 ULTA Beauty purchase.
And, to get the free gift I needed to spend $19.50, then this was $10, so I ended up just getting two of them.

opening.argument: The pressure cues matter in combination. The headline says to act right now; the description makes the offer time- and quantity-limited and supplies a link for getting it online. The speaker also repeats a claimed $88 value for a gift tied to a $19.50 spend, then urges viewers to run to the store. That is a particularly forceful way to move someone from a reward claim to an immediate purchase. The qualifying terms are present, but they do not independently verify the stated value or availability.

citations.quote: GET 10 FREE Gifts @ ULTA Beauty RIGHT NOW!!!
Offer is valid now through 4/4/20 or while quantities last.
★GET yours in store or online at : https://www.ulta.com/gifts-with-purchase?N=26wy
I believe Ulta Beauty valued this gift bag at $88

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the threshold and review, but neither verifies the value claim or removes the urgency surrounding the purchase. Saying the offer is still available on the website is the speaker's assertion, not independent confirmation within the material. The question is whether the reward pitch pushes viewers to act on those assertions, even though the purchase condition is stated.

citations.quote: I believe Ulta Beauty valued this gift bag at $88
on Ulta's website it is still available
Offer is valid now through 4/4/20 or while quantities last.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Urgency and an estimated gift value do not establish deception. The description gives both the purchase threshold and the offer's end condition, and its link is presented as a store gift-with-purchase page. The speaker even qualifies the value with 'I believe.' The opening identifies sales language, but no evidence that the terms, value claim, or availability were false.

citations.quote: Right now you can get a FREE 10 piece gift with any $19.50 ULTA Beauty purchase. Offer is valid now through 4/4/20 or while quantities last.
★GET yours in store or online at : https://www.ulta.com/gifts-with-purchase?N=26wy
I believe Ulta Beauty valued this gift bag at $88

opening.argument: The try-on is also a route into the offer. The speaker opens by inviting viewers to review the products, repeatedly stresses that the items were free, praises particular results, and closes with a direct instruction to buy something to get the bundle. Those evaluations can make the reward feel tangible and worthwhile before the purchase request arrives. A judge should assess the full sequence as persuasion toward the gift-for-purchase offer, not treat the review format alone as proof that the solicitation is harmless.

citations.quote: I made a trip to Ulta Beauty and walked away with 10 free beauty products that we are going to try out and review together.
Overall, I'm very pleased with these products that I received, remember for FREE, zero dollars did I pay for any of this stuff
this lipstick this lipstick is phenomenal
If your store has it, you need to run down to Ulta, something for $19 and get this whole stuff for free!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that products are tried on; that is precisely why the eventual purchase appeal may carry weight. Nor does the stated threshold settle how the repeated 'free' framing affects viewers. The review and the solicitation are connected: after evaluating the items, the speaker tells viewers to go obtain the gift through a purchase.

citations.quote: Overall, I'm very pleased with these products that I received, remember for FREE, zero dollars did I pay for any of this stuff
If your store has it, you need to run down to Ulta, something for $19 and get this whole stuff for free!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A review can encourage a purchase without being a scam. This one includes unfavorable judgments as well as praise: the speaker says the brush is too flimsy and the darker eyeshadows lack depth. She also explicitly identifies the brow pencil as a purchase made to qualify for the gifts. The opening shows promotion, but not a false reward or a concealed participation requirement.
